title: Bank Security Department SMS Alert

scenario.subject: Suspicious Card Activity
scenario.body: CHASE FRAUD ALERT: Did you authorize a $948.50 charge at WALMART ONLINE on 09/10? Reply NO to stop this payment or call our fraud hotline immediately at 1-844-555-0182.
scenario.context: Simulated SMS smishing leading to telephone boiler room.

options.text: SAFE — Reply NO or call the number right away to stop the charge
SUSPICIOUS — Call the verified phone number printed on the back of your physical credit card
SCAM — Smishing lure designed to connect you directly to a fraudulent call center agent

indicators.description: Toll-free number in SMS belongs to scammers, not Chase Bank
High charge ($948.50) to trigger immediate impulsive phone call
Lacks official bank shortcode; sends direct unverified phone number

explanation: Bank impersonation via SMS (Smishing) provides fake 1-800 phone numbers. When victims call, a convincing scammer posing as a fraud agent asks for full debit card numbers, PINs, and one-time passcodes under the pretense of 'reversing' the charge.
hints: Where is the only 100% safe place to find your bank's real telephone number?
Why should you never call phone numbers sent inside unsolicited text messages?
Legitimate banks never ask for your PIN or online password over the phone.
learningObjective: Never call phone numbers sent via SMS; always use the number printed on your physical card.
consequenceChain: You called the 1-844 number and spoke with a fake fraud agent
Agent asked you to 'read back the 6-digit verification code sent to your phone'
Agent used the code to authorize an instant Zelle wire transfer draining $2,000
recoverySteps: Call legitimate bank fraud hotline using number on back of card
Request immediate freeze on online banking and associated debit cards
File police report for grand theft / wire fraud

title: Official Bank Statement

scenario.message:
Dear Customer,

Your monthly account statement for October is now available. You can view it by logging into your account through our official website or mobile app.

Thank you for banking with us.
scenario.context: A regular monthly bank statement notification.

options.text: SAFE - Routine bank notification
SCAM - Fake statement phishing attempt

indicators.description: Tells you to log in through the official app rather than providing a link.

explanation: This is safe because it does not provide a direct link for you to click. Legitimate banks often send notifications like this and advise you to log in securely via their known official website or app.

title: WhatsApp Remote App Tester High-Pay Job

scenario.subject: Remote Part-Time Opportunity
scenario.body: Hello! I am Elena from Adecco HR Recruitment. We found your resume on LinkedIn! We have an urgent remote job: rate 30 mobile apps daily for 30-45 minutes and earn $300-$800/day paid directly in USDT or PayPal. No experience required! Reply YES to begin your onboarding training.
scenario.context: Classic task scam (task-based optimization scam) requiring upfront deposit to unlock earnings.

options.text: SAFE — Great flexible side hustle
SUSPICIOUS — Verify job listing on official Adecco career website
SCAM — Task Scam requiring victims to deposit their own money into fake crypto platforms to complete tasks

indicators.description: Unrealistic compensation ($300-800/day for 30 mins) for low-skill tasks
Compensation promised in cryptocurrency / USDT
Recruiter contacts via unsolicited WhatsApp/Telegram with foreign country code

explanation: Task Scams trick victims into performing simple tasks on a fake website. Initially, small 'profits' can be withdrawn to build trust. Then, the platform freezes your funds and demands thousands of dollars in 'recharge deposits' to unlock your balance.
hints: Is $800 for 30 minutes of app rating realistic in the real economy?
Do legitimate corporate recruiters reach out cold on WhatsApp using international numbers?
Why do task scams require victims to deposit money before they can withdraw earnings?
learningObjective: Recognize Task Scams and unrealistic remote employment offers delivered over chat apps.
consequenceChain: You completed rating tasks and deposited $500 'workbench recharge'
Platform showed fake balance of $1,800 but blocked withdrawals
Support demanded $1,500 'tax clearance fee' to unlock the funds
recoverySteps: Cease all contact and do NOT send any additional deposit funds
Report phone number and WhatsApp profile to WhatsApp Anti-Fraud
Beware of 'recovery scammers' claiming they can hack back stolen funds

title: Friend/Family Emergency Bail Text

scenario.subject: Emergency!
scenario.body: Hey, it's Alex! My phone dropped in the pool and broke so I'm texting from a stranger's phone. I'm in huge trouble in Mexico, my rental car got impounded and the police need $650 for the release fee or they'll detain me overnight. Please Zelle $650 to alex.bail.transit@fastmail.com right now, I'll pay you back the second I get home tomorrow! Don't tell mom, she'll panic!
scenario.context: Family emergency impersonation scam leveraging secrecy and late-night panic.

options.text: SAFE — Send the money immediately to save your friend from jail
SUSPICIOUS — Call Alex's original phone number, call mutual friends/family, or ask a personal question only Alex knows
SCAM — Emergency impersonation scam using panic, isolation, and secrecy to prevent verification

indicators.description: 'Don't tell mom' isolate victim from third-party rational check
'Broke my phone' excuse explains why stranger's number is texting
Demands instant irreversible payment via Zelle / gift card / wire

explanation: Emergency impersonation scams exploit love, empathy, and urgency. Scammers deliberately tell you 'don't tell anyone' to isolate you from people who would point out the scam. Always verify out-of-band with a secret question only your real friend knows.
hints: Why is the sender urgently demanding you NOT tell other family members?
What happens if you call your friend's regular phone number directly?
Ask a question that only the real friend could answer (e.g. 'What is my dog's middle name?').
learningObjective: Overcome emotional manipulation in family emergency scams through out-of-band verification.
consequenceChain: You transferred $650 via Zelle in late-night panic
Next morning you spoke with the real Alex, who was asleep in his own bed at home
Zelle transfer was final and non-refundable
recoverySteps: Contact Zelle / your bank to file fraud report
Establish a family 'safe word / code phrase' for genuine emergencies
Block the scammer's phone number

title: Crypto 'Pig Butchering' (Sha Zhu Pan) Relationship

scenario.sender: Chloe (Met on Dating App 2 weeks ago)
scenario.subject: Our Future Together
scenario.body: Good morning dear! My uncle is a chief financial analyst in Singapore and shared private insider signals on ETH liquidity mining node contracts today. Look at my screenshot — I made $14,200 just this morning! We can buy our dream house together sooner if you open a VIP node on global-defi-liquidity.vip. I will guide you step by step!
scenario.context: Sha Zhu Pan (Pig Butchering) romance-financial investment scam.

options.text: SAFE — She is sharing valuable insider family investment advice out of love
SUSPICIOUS — Consult an independent certified financial planner
SCAM — Pig Butchering romance-investment scam routing deposits to an offshore criminal syndicate

indicators.description: Romance grooming followed by introduction of high-yield crypto platform
Custom fake trading platform controlled entirely by scammers
Guaranteed 200%+ returns on insider crypto arbitrage

explanation: Pig Butchering (Sha Zhu Pan) scams build romantic or friendly trust over weeks before steering victims to fake cryptocurrency investment platforms. The platform manipulates charts to show fake profits, but victims can never withdraw their real money.
hints: Why did an online romantic acquaintance suddenly pivot to cryptocurrency investments?
Who controls the website 'global-defi-liquidity.vip'?
If someone had guaranteed insider market secrets, why would they share them with casual online contacts?
learningObjective: Identify Pig Butchering romance-investment grooming and recognize fraudulent trading platforms.
consequenceChain: You invested $5,000 into the liquidity platform and saw balance climb to $28,000
Attempted withdrawal was blocked pending a $6,000 'anti-money laundering tax'
Romance partner disappeared and blocked you across all social media
recoverySteps: Accept that the money sent to the crypto addresses is gone and refuse all further demands
File detailed report with FBI IC3 and local law enforcement
Seek emotional support from trusted friends and counseling services

title: Immediate Electric Utility Disconnection Threat

scenario.subject: URGENT DISCONNECTION NOTICE
scenario.body: FINAL NOTICE: Your electricity service at this address is scheduled for remote disconnection within 45 MINUTES due to past due balance of $187.20. Technicians are en route. To cancel shutoff order immediately, call dispatch at 1-800-555-4921 and pay balance via GreenDot MoneyPak / barcode cashier.
scenario.context: Utility disconnection scam targeting homes and small businesses during peak hours.

options.text: SAFE — Rush to store to purchase prepaid card and prevent power outage
SUSPICIOUS — Check utility account balance on the official power company website/app
SCAM — Utility shutoff scam demanding untraceable prepaid vouchers/cards under extreme urgency

indicators.description: Demands payment via prepaid cash cards (MoneyPak, vanilla reload, gift cards)
45-minute cutoff deadline to prevent victim from checking bills
Regulated utilities are legally required to send written postal notices weeks before disconnection

explanation: Regulated utilities never demand payment via prepaid vouchers, gift cards, or cryptocurrency. They are legally mandated to send multiple written delinquency notices by postal mail over several weeks before shutting off power.
hints: Do legitimate power companies demand GreenDot MoneyPak cards or retail gift cards?
Can utilities shut off electricity with only 45 minutes of SMS notice?
Check your balance directly on your power company's official billing portal.
learningObjective: Recognize utility disconnection scams and remember that gift cards/MoneyPaks are never acceptable utility payment methods.
consequenceChain: You bought $187.20 MoneyPak card and read numbers over phone to fake technician
Scammer cashed out voucher within seconds
Your legitimate utility bill remained unchanged and power was never in danger
recoverySteps: Contact the power company on official billing statement number to confirm account status
Report scam telephone number to state public utility commission
File consumer fraud complaint with Federal Trade Commission (FTC)

title: Apartment Rental Security Deposit Wire

scenario.subject: Luxury Downtown 2-Bed Apartment - Application Approved
scenario.body: Congratulations! Your rental application for the downtown penthouse ($1,200/mo, all utilities included) is approved! I am currently in London on a Doctors Without Borders mission, so I cannot show the unit in person. If you wire the $1,200 first month + $1,200 deposit via Western Union today, my local courier will FedEx the front door keys to you tomorrow morning.
scenario.context: Simulated fake rental listing using stolen real estate photos and remote landlord story.

options.text: SAFE — Wire the deposit immediately to lock down this below-market rent
SUSPICIOUS — Tour the physical apartment in person with a licensed agent before paying anything
SCAM — Classic phantom rental scam where photos are stolen from Zillow and keys never arrive

indicators.description: 'Missionary/Doctor overseas' story excuses inability to show the physical apartment
Luxury downtown penthouse offered at 50% below real market rate
Demands wire transfer (Western Union / Zelle) prior to in-person walkthrough or lease signing

explanation: Phantom rental scams steal high-end photos from real estate sites (Zillow/Redfin) and list them at bargain prices. The 'landlord is overseas' excuse explains why they can't meet in person. Never send deposits for properties you have not walked through in person.
hints: Why is a luxury downtown penthouse priced at half the market average?
Why is the landlord claiming to be out of the country on a charitable mission?
Never transfer funds before inspecting an apartment in person and verifying property ownership.
learningObjective: Prevent real estate rental fraud and reject deposit payments without in-person property inspection.
consequenceChain: You wired $2,400 via Western Union to the overseas address
You arrived at the apartment address with your moving truck
The real resident opened the door in confusion; the listing was completely fraudulent
recoverySteps: Contact Western Union fraud department immediately to attempt wire intercept
File police report for grand larceny
Report fake listing to the rental website hosting the fraudulent advertisement

title: Wrong Number 'Accidental' Friendship Grooming

scenario.subject: Golf tournament dinner
scenario.body: Hi David, is our tee time still confirmed for 9 AM tomorrow with Michael at Pebble Beach? Let me know so I can reserve the caddie.
scenario.context: Wrong Number / Wrong Contact social engineering probe to initiate rapport.

options.text: Reply: 'Sorry, wrong number, I am not David' and continue chatting if they say 'Oh excuse me, you seem very polite!'
Ignore / Block the number — Scammers send deliberate wrong number texts to find active numbers and initiate Pig Butchering grooming
Forward your own personal contact information

indicators.description: Deliberate wrong-number message crafted to sound wealthy and polite
First stage of social engineering grooming funnel (Pig Butchering / Crypto lure)
Any response confirms telephone number is active to spam databases

explanation: These 'accidental' texts are completely deliberate. If you reply 'wrong number', the scammer responds with flattering messages like 'Oh, so sorry for disturbing you! You seem like such a kind person, let's be friends!' to begin weeks-long financial grooming.
hints: Why are thousands of people receiving nearly identical 'wrong number' messages about golf, dinner, or pet grooming?
What happens when you reply to an unknown mass-smishing sender?
The safest action for unsolicited stranger messages is to delete and block.
learningObjective: Recognize deliberate 'wrong number' chat lures designed to start social grooming funnels.
consequenceChain: You politely replied 'wrong number' and chatted for 3 weeks
Stranger built rapport and introduced an offshore precious metals investment platform
You invested life savings which was stolen by organized scam syndicate
recoverySteps: Block and report number as spam on your mobile operating system
Do not engage with strangers who attempt to continue conversations after wrong number mistakes
Enable carrier spam call & text filtering

title: SIM Swap 2FA Hijack Warning Probe

scenario.subject: Carrier Account Update
scenario.body: CARRIER NOTIFICATION: A request to transfer your phone number to a new eSIM device was initiated at 3:44 PM. If this was NOT you, reply 'CANCEL' within 10 minutes or call customer care.
scenario.context: Real carrier warning message during active SIM swap attack in progress.

options.text: Ignore it — Assume it's just another spam text
IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY ACTION — Call carrier official fraud hotline immediately from another phone or store to block the active SIM swap
Reply 'CANCEL' and go back to work

indicators.description: Attacker is actively socially engineering your mobile carrier to seize your phone number
Legitimate shortcode notification warning of imminent cellular disconnect
Victim has minutes before cellular service drops and 2FA SMS goes to attacker

explanation: Unlike fake scam texts, this message is a REAL warning from your legitimate mobile carrier that an attacker is actively transferring your number to their device (SIM Swap). You have minutes to call carrier fraud support before your phone loses service and your bank accounts are accessed.
hints: Is this message sent from an official carrier shortcode (e.g. 22000)?
What happens if an attacker successfully ports your phone number to their eSIM?
Why must you immediately contact your carrier to place a fraud lock on your account?
learningObjective: Distinguish between fake phishing texts and real carrier security alerts during active SIM swap attacks.
consequenceChain: You ignored the warning thinking it was spam
Phone display changed to 'No Service / SOS Only'
Attacker used intercepted SMS OTPs to reset passwords on your email, cryptocurrency, and bank accounts
recoverySteps: Immediately call carrier from a landline or walk into an official carrier retail store with photo ID
Request immediate port freeze and reverse the unauthorized eSIM swap
Set a mandatory Verbal Port-Out PIN Passcode on your cellular account

title: Fake Tech Support 'Windows Defender Alert' Lockup

scenario.subject: CRITICAL: Trojan.Spyware.Banker.88 Detected
scenario.body:
YOUR COMPUTER HAS BEEN BLOCKED DUE TO VIRUS INFECTION.

Error Code: #0x80070002
Do NOT restart or turn off your computer. Your registry keys, passwords, and banking data are being transmitted to a foreign server.

Call Microsoft Certified Engineers immediately at 1-888-555-0199 for instant remote unlock.
scenario.context: Full-screen browser lockup scam with audio siren and fake helpline.

options.text: SAFE — Call 1-888-555-0199 to have Microsoft technicians clean the computer remotely
SUSPICIOUS — Unplug the power cable immediately
SCAM — Browser lockup JavaScript fullscreen trick; press Escape, force-quit browser in Task Manager, and never call the number

indicators.description: Uses JavaScript requestFullScreen() to fake operating system lockup
Microsoft never displays phone numbers on error screens or asks users to call engineers
Designed to bait victims into allowing remote desktop control (AnyDesk/TeamViewer)

explanation: Tech support popups use JavaScript fullscreen tricks, looping audio alarms, and cursor lock to make you think Windows is frozen. Microsoft never includes toll-free telephone numbers in operating system alerts. Simply close the browser tab using Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc).
hints: Does Microsoft or Apple ever put customer support phone numbers on error screens?
How can you close a locked browser window using Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc)?
Never grant remote desktop control to someone you contacted from an internet popup.
learningObjective: Escape full-screen browser lockup traps without calling fraudulent tech support phone numbers.
consequenceChain: You called the 1-888 number and let the technician connect via UltraViewer
Scammer opened Syskey / command prompt, typed 'TREE', and claimed your computer was ruined
Demanded $499 in Apple gift cards for a '5-year security license'
recoverySteps: Force close browser with Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc)
Clear browser cookies and cache
Install reputable ad blocker extension (e.g. uBlock Origin)

title: Unclaimed Postal Lottery Winning Check

scenario.subject: Winner Selected!
scenario.body: CONGRATULATIONS! Your mobile phone number was drawn as the 2nd Prize Winner in the North American Consumer Sweepstakes ($250,000.00 cash). A cashier's check of $4,500 is being mailed to cover your initial state gaming taxes. Deposit this check and wire back $3,800 to our disbursement officer to release your $250,000 grand prize!

options.text: SAFE — Deposit the $4,500 cashier check at your bank and wire the $3,800 tax
SUSPICIOUS — Wait 3 days for the check to clear before wiring money
SCAM — Counterfeit check scam; the check will bounce after 1-2 weeks and you will be held legally liable for the $3,800 wired money

indicators.description: Fake cashier's check appears to clear initially under federal funds availability rules, then bounces days later
Legitimate lotteries deduct taxes directly from winnings; they never ask winners to wire taxes back
You cannot win a sweepstakes or lottery that you never bought a ticket for

explanation: Federal banking regulations require banks to make check funds available within 1-2 business days, but true verification of an out-of-state cashier's check takes weeks. When the counterfeit check inevitably bounces, the bank claws back the full $4,500 from your account, and any money you wired to the scammer is gone forever.
hints: Can you win a lottery contest that you never entered?
Why does a check appearing as 'available funds' in your banking app not mean it has truly cleared?
Legitimate lotteries never require winners to wire money to receive payouts.
learningObjective: Understand counterfeit check clearing mechanics and avoid advance-fee lottery scams.
consequenceChain: You deposited the fake check and wired $3,800 to the claims officer
10 days later the bank identified the check as counterfeit and deducted $4,500 from your account
Your bank account was left severely overdrawn and flagged for check fraud
recoverySteps: Contact bank branch manager to explain you were the victim of counterfeit check fraud
File report with US Postal Inspection Service (USPIS)
Never wire money from deposited checks from strangers
